subject: Renewal: Throughput uplift, new tiering, and fallback guarantee
messages:
From: Liam Chen <liam@cloudcart.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Priya Raj <priya@cloudcart.com>
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning and throughput needs

Hi Jasmine,

We’re starting budget planning for H2 and want to lock in a hosted path that keeps latency stable as we scale checkout personalization across EU and US. Current usage is ~45M tokens/month; expected to spike to 120M by Q4 after we roll out dynamic content.

Key asks:
- Can Redwood commit to a plan that scales to ~150M tokens/mo by October with predictable per-token rates?
- We need a fallback mechanism (model downgrades) that preserves 95th pctl latency targets without catastrophic cost spikes if we hit bursts.
- Any early renewal incentives or credits for a 12-month commitment?

Also copying Priya (ops) who owns procurement. Happy to jump on a call this week.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam Chen
Head of Platform
CloudCart
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Chen <liam@cloudcart.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning and throughput needs

Hi Liam — great to hear from you, and congrats on the roadmap momentum.

Short answer: yes, we can design a hosted commit and tiering plan to cover 120–150M tokens/month while giving you deterministic unit economics and an automated fallback that protects latency and softens rate spikes.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick scoping call (30m) to confirm Q4 traffic shape and peak-minute rates — are you free Thu 10th 11am PT?
2) We’ll circulate a draft SOW and a pricing worksheet showing: baseline commit, burst pocket, and a fallback plan that automatically routes to a compact model with a 10–15% quality/regression budget but preserves 95th pctl latency.
3) If the economics look good, we’ll prepare a DocuSign-ready SOW + a 12-month incentive (3% credit on committed spend for early sign).

I’ve looped in Vanessa (renewals/ops) and Karthik (pricing/infra) to start the internal sizing.

—Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal planning and throughput needs — internal sizing

Team — putting preliminary numbers here so we can converge before we send anything to CloudCart. Attachment: pricing_model_v3.xlsx (stub)

Notes / assumptions:
- Current observed 45M tokens/mo (baseline).
- Forecasted steady-state: 120M tokens/mo by Oct; peak day up to 6x baseline for marketing bursts.

Draft proposal (high level):
- Baseline commit: 100M tokens/mo at tier rate $0.0009/token (hosted model family A).
- Tiered burst band: 25M tokens/mo burst pocket at $0.0012/token.
- Auto-burst fallback: additional demand beyond burst pocket routed to a compact-family model (90% token parity on high-frequency prompts) with a guaranteed 95th pctl latency < 280ms; rate: $0.0006/token for routed tokens to give a soft-cost cap.
- Capacity guardrail: soft throttle at sustained 5x baseline, with 72-hour notice to avoid sudden throttles.

Open items:
- SLA exception note for the fallback model (we need to document expected quality variance) — add SLA-exceptions.docx.
- Do we want to include a 3% early renewal credit or increase to 5% if they commit 12 months?

Ben — can you validate GPU slot commitment and whether Dedicated burst capacity is needed for predictable peak handling?

- Vanessa
Renewals Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal planning and throughput needs — pricing & fallback mechanics

Good notes. A few engineering constraints and a suggested safe configuration:

Engineering constraints:
- Model family A (high-fidelity) runs best on contiguous A100 pools; switching to compact-family involves model variant with 4-bit quant and different kernel selection — cold-start for KV cache rebuild is ~250ms on warm-up.
- Continuous batching and KV caching will handle burst smoothing for most traffic shapes, but 6x sudden spike can still pressure memory.

Suggested commercial configuration:
- Commit ladder: 100M -> 125M -> 150M tokens per month with stepped per-token discounts at each step. (We’ll show a 3-tier pricing table in the worksheet.)
- Fallback trigger: automatic when 1-minute rolling QPS pushes latency above 95th pctl target for 3 consecutive minutes OR when quota consumption crosses 110% of burst pocket in a 24-hour window.
- Fallback behavior: route new sessions to compact-family + circuit-breaker that prevents model switching more than once per 5 minutes for a user session.

Operational asks for SOW:
- Add a clause for a 7-day pro-rata credit if fallback routing is invoked for more than 48 cumulative hours in a 30-day window.
- Include an onboarding runbook item: CloudCart to provide a 50-example prompt set for quality verification of compact-family before go-live.

If these look reasonable I’ll author the SOW language and hand to Legal for redlines.

—Karthik
Director, Model Onboarding | Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Chen <liam@cloudcart.com>
Cc: Priya Raj <priya@cloudcart.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed renewal & throughput uplift — SOW and next steps

Hi Liam / Priya — thanks for the quick sync yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is a single-package proposal and the SOW (SOW_CloudCart_v3.pdf stub). Also linking a DocuSign envelope for signature: https://www.docusign.com/CLD-CC-98765

Highlights:
- Term: 12 months (start date on signature).
- Commit ladder: 100M tokens/mo guaranteed baseline for months 1–3, step to 125M/mo months 4–6, and 150M/mo months 7–12 (prorated on partial months).
- Burst pocket: 25M tokens/mo at elevated burst rate.
- Fallback guarantee: automated routing to compact-family model with documented quality caveat; if fallback routing exceeds 48 cumulative hours in a rolling 30-day window, CloudCart receives a pro-rata credit for impacted usage (7-day credit).
- Pricing: blended effective rate shown in the attached worksheet; 3% early-renewal credit applied on signed annual commitment.

Please review the SOW and the worksheet. If this looks good, sign via DocuSign and the legal team will push final redlines. If you want a higher early-renewal credit, we can propose 5% for an accelerated signature before May 20.

Attachments (stubs): SOW_CloudCart_v3.pdf, pricing_model_v3.xlsx

Best,
—Jasmine
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Liam Chen <liam@cloudcart.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Raj <priya@cloudcart.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed renewal & throughput uplift — SOW and next steps

Jasmine — thanks, this looks actionable.

Two quick items before signing:
1) Can you confirm the burst pocket is usable across regions (we have EU-heavy traffic)?
2) If fallback is invoked, will the compact-family routing be visible in request logs (we need to flag debug traces to our engineers)?

Assuming answers are OK we’ll sign today and route the DocuSign to procurement.

Thanks,
Liam
